items.problem: `efficiency`. `collect` keeps walking the whole queue after the collected headcount reached `max_players`, though no later entry can fit, and `run_queue` calls it once per match, so one `matchmaker_tick` over one queue is quadratic in the queue size and blocks the event loop of all `/realtime` connections and requests of that server instance. Run path: `run_tick` to `run_queue` to `collect`, growing amount: entries of one queue. Entries pile up behind an e0 that has no partner until its `match_wait` ends, because step 5 ends the queue at e0. Measured with `run_queue` directly, `max_players` 2, same ratings: 8000 entries 130 ms, 16000 entries 580 ms, 32000 entries 2583 ms. With `if (count === rule.max_players) break;` after the placement in a temporary copy: 32000 entries 229 ms, and `matching.test.ts` and `queue-rules.test.ts` pass on SQLite

With `matchmaker.frameReadTimeoutMs` 0, one partial frame from an unauthenticated client throws out of the socket `data` listener. The schema allows 0 (settings/core-settings.schema.json:689), and `frame_time_limit` calls `server_time.network_time_limit(0n)`, which throws when ms is less than 1 (server/core/server-time/network_time_limit.ts:9). `WebSocketConnection.#read` reaches it through `#time_frame` (server/core/matchmaker/websocket.ts:167, :196). Reproduced on a stream with the real `WebSocketConnection` and `network_time_limit`: `socket.emit('data', Buffer.from([0x82]))` threw `network_time_limit: ms 0 is below 1`. server/core has no `uncaughtException` handler, so a real socket would end the server process; that last step was not run. `matchmaker.helloTimeoutMs` 0 (settings/core-settings.schema.json:697) throws the same way at server/core/matchmaker/realtime.ts:856, where the catch in `upgrade` (server/core/routing/pipeline.ts:823) destroys the socket, so every `/realtime` connection fails after its handshake. The range did not cause this: it raised six other keys to 1, and server/core/routing/tests/settings-minimum.test.ts only starts a server, with no connection, so it passes with both keys at 0. The spec writes no range for either key; the same cause is D5 of records/review-debt/spec-matchmaker.json.
